approachGroups._note: Round 21. Named sets of outside nodes that say where a through car comes from or is going, in words a resident uses. Gates are placed by the first rule that matches (street names and classes at the gate, whether trips can only enter or only leave, and the compass bearing in degrees clockwise from north from the study area's center to the gate). Other outside nodes take the group of the nearest surface gate (ASSUMPTION). `overrides` (node id to group id) fix gates the rules place wrongly. `sets` are named unions. The reserved id `study-area` stands for the nodes inside the study area.

throughIntents._note: Cut-through reasons. Hypotheses about why a car crosses the study area without an end in it, in words a resident uses. A through trip that uses a residential or service street of the study area is tallied under the first reason that fits, in this order: the SR-24 on-ramp it will use (ramps are derived from the network, tools/lib/ramps.ts; the car's planned route at the moment it is counted), the off-ramp it came by (the links it has driven), or, for a trip that uses no ramp, the first reason whose fromGroups holds its origin group and whose toGroups holds its destination group; any other goes under Other. Groups and sets are those of approachGroups. basis `observed`: a volunteer or agency count of a turning movement, a freeway share or a ramp limits how many cars the model sends this way; where they come from and why is still the model's assumption. basis `assumed`: no count limits it. `avoids` is the arterial the trip would otherwise use on the shortest free-flow route with the side streets closed (an assumption of the calibrate report, not a driver survey). A ramp reason is listed for each ramp that carries about 3% or more of the PM peak's through cars; the rest go under Other on-ramps and Other off-ramps.

intents.note: Counted turns from Alcatraz Ave onto Hillegass Ave and Colby St southbound (the volunteer count of Feb 25, 2025) and the freeway share of those blocks limit how many cars use these side streets to reach this ramp, and the ramp's own volume is fitted to its Caltrans count. Where the cars start (Berkeley and College Ave, or Telegraph Ave and the west side of Alcatraz Ave) and that they are bypassing Telegraph Ave are assumptions; the card lists where the model's cars start.

intents.label: Other on-ramps
intents.note: Through cars bound for any SR-24 on-ramp not listed above. A ramp's volume is fitted to its Caltrans count where one was matched and is an assumed default where none was. No count says how many of these cars cross the study area on side streets.

Counted northbound exits at Alcatraz Ave from Colby St (164 an hour, 163 of them turning) and Hillegass Ave (109 an hour, 97 of them turning) and the share of those blocks' trips that came from a freeway (47% for each street) limit how many of these cars use the side streets. The ramp's volume is fitted to its Caltrans count and its split with the other Claremont Ave off-ramp to the counts downstream of each. Where the cars are bound (Berkeley, Alcatraz Ave west or the hills) is an assumption; the card lists where the model's cars go.

intents.label: Other off-ramps
intents.note: Through cars that came from any SR-24 off-ramp not listed above. A ramp's volume is fitted to its Caltrans count where one was matched and is an assumed default where none was. No count says how many of these cars cross the study area on side streets.

calibration.note: Not calibrated: PM through cars on Hillegass Ave and Colby St southbound are still above the counted ranges.
calibration.caveat: Round 32, PM peak: through cars on Hillegass Ave southbound 137 an hour (counted range 79 to 120) and Colby St southbound 128 (39 to 117); Colby St northbound 148 (102 to 145) is just above its range and Hillegass Ave northbound 96 at the top of its own (48 to 95). Three of the four headline freeway shares are within 10 points. Gridlock removals are 0.8 an hour in the PM peak over ten seeds, inside the limit of 1, but 1.4 on another ten; the AM peak and midday have none. Simulated drivers now change lanes along a block to pass a waiting left-turner or a blocked lane, and closely spaced signals, such as the three at the SR-24 ramps on Telegraph Ave, share a cycle with greens timed to the travel time between them. Both made Telegraph Ave faster and cut the through cars on the side streets. Feeding the simulated delays back into the demand brings every counted side-street block and headline share into range, but queues on Claremont Ave northbound at Ashby Ave then spill into the hillside streets, so that demand is not used. The left-turn pocket size, the lane-change settings and the distance for joint signal timing are assumptions. Lane counts on Stanford Ave, 51st St and Telegraph Ave just north of 55th St were corrected from map tags and still need a field check. The recent PM count stations pass GEH 5 at 76 of 92 fitted (83%) and 13 of 24 held out of the fit (54%); AM 67 of 77 (87%) and 14 of 19 (74%). Almost all recent stations come from one hour of one day of resident volunteer counting (February 25, 2025). Midday has no counts and is checked for stability only. Treat through-car figures, and changes between scenarios, as model output that does not yet match the counts.

Field observation by a resident, relayed by the project lead (2026-11-15): the northbound Claremont Ave approach at Ashby Ave has a left-turn arrow, so its left turn onto Ashby Ave is protected (DATA for the phasing). The 2010 PM Synchro worksheet of [SafewayCollege-DEIR2011] runs the two Claremont Ave approaches as split phases (northbound 17.0 s, southbound 17.5 s of a 100 s cycle) and codes the northbound approach as two lanes with no left-turn lane, which fits. ASSUMPTION pending a timing sheet: the approach runs in a phase of its own in every period (protected-only, not protected-permissive), and the cycle and greens follow the flows like any other modeled signal; the other approaches' phasing, the pocket length and the timing are not observed
